page.layout: One printed page. Running head at top (centred). Main text in one column, paragraphs running down the page. Below the text: a centred heading "EXERC. XXI.", a second centred heading in small capitals "DE SCABIE, ET VTRVM" with an italic line "sit totius substantiæ morbus?", then a paragraph opening with a large woodcut initial "M" and ending with "causis.", set flush right. No marginal notes. No catchword or signature.

main_text.p: rius in quo natura omnino est uicta, aut adeo imbecillis reddita, ut nullam amplius in putrescentia excrementa ad optimum moliri posit tranfmutationem. Quæ uero in uenis confiftit putredo, mutatio est fup-purationi proportione refpondens: in qua fedimentum in urinis apparens idem est, quod pus in abscesibus: non quod tamen fimplex ueraq; sit coctio, sed quod (quemadmodum inquit Galenus) concoctionis aliquid contineat. Idcirco non absoluta est putredo. Simplex enim putredo nullam unquam admittit coctionem, nihilq; in ea assimilatur secundum substantiam, aut qualitates. Quo putredinis genere fiunt gangrenæ & sphaceli, atq; lethales febres, in quibus corrupti humores nullam unquam assequuntur concoctionem. Quamobrem partes, quibus superueniunt gangrenę & sphaceli abscindi necesse est.
main_text.head: EXERC. XXI.
DE SCABIE, ET VTRVM sit totius substantiæ morbus?
main_text.p: MOrbis totius substantiæ scabiem annumerat Fernelius capite undecimo, libri secundi, de Abditis rerum causis.

page.notes: The page is a little worn; "posit" in the first line is printed as "possit"-like form and read here as "posit" with [?] not needed. Line "rius in quo" is the start of the paragraph continued from the previous page. The drop-cap "M" is a woodcut initial joined to "Orbis" as printed; transcribed as "MOrbis". Printed spelling "Putredo"/"putredinis" and "gangrenæ" retained as printed. Printed "uicta" and "uero" kept with u as printed in the scan's spelling.
